articleTitle: Geomatrical Theory of Diffraction(GTD) Part I: Foundation of the theory
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society Newsletter
abstract: This article is intended to people interested in electromagnetic high-frequency diffraction by perfectly and imperfectly conducting objects. It describes the physical foundations and postulates of the Geometrical Theory of Diffraction as formulated originally by Keller. A great emphasis is devoted to the mathematical foundations of the theory which permits to elucidate its possibilities and limitations and to introduce later developments and improvements (See Part II of this article). For each diffraction process, the most important formulas of GTD are presented with comments concerning their utility in practical applications and a review of available diffraction coefficients.

articleTitle: The Swiss EMP concept of general defense
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society Newsletter
abstract: The Swiss Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) committee, established in 1978 to study large scale effects of EMP, especially of high-altitude nuclear explosions, concluded their findings in an EMP concept. In this concept, embedded in the comprehensive concept of general defense and approved by the federal authorities in 1983, a set of governing principles is outlined to reach the following goals in case of EMP impacts on the country: - Continuation of the government's functions - Assured existence of the population - Maintained capacity of military defense. There is no question about EMP creating damages and imposing severe limitations in many fields. However, by carefully selecting and applying protective measures - required especially for the most essential systems of public information, communications, power generation and distribution, transports etc. - the country gets a real chance to survive EMP situations. To support the concept furthermore a legal regulation has been prepared. Some important issues of the EMP concept are presented.

articleTitle: Geometrical Theory of Diffraction(GTD) Part II: Extensions and future trends of the theory
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society Newsletter
abstract: An analysis of the extensions and improvements of GTD since its early time is given. Especially the theoretical foundations of two powerful methods, namely the Boundary Layer Method and the Uniform Asymptotic Expansion Method, are outlined. Aspects of these theories which are of growing interest at present, for solving electromagentic diffraction and radiation problems are pointed out. The resulting solutions are described in a general framework including perfectly conducting and imperfectly conducting objects condition. Their limitations are discussed and indications for further improvements are given. Some new non published results on higher-order edges and coated metallic bodies are also included. The author concludes with a brief description of future trends in the development of GTD.

abstract: The present status of MMIC-fed phased-arrays, is reviewed through the results of a workshop on the subject. Problem areas are identified and recommendations for future developments are presented. The paper addresses five aspects of the MMIC phased-array design: array architecture, MMIC-to-radiating -element interface, RF signal distribution, performance monitoring and fault isolation, and computer -aided design tools for MMIC arrays.
